nameStory: This little moss gets its name from the distinctive gray-green cushions it forms on rocks and walls. The word 'pulvinata' comes from Latin meaning 'cushioned' or 'pillow-like,' perfectly describing how this moss creates soft, rounded mounds that look like tiny gray pillows scattered across stone surfaces.
description: Grey-cushioned grimmia is a small moss that forms dense, rounded cushions on rocks, walls, and concrete surfaces. Each cushion is typically about the size of a quarter to a silver dollar, made up of tightly packed stems with small, narrow leaves. When dry, the cushions appear grayish-green and feel firm to the touch, but when wet they become a brighter green and soften considerably. This hardy little moss can be found worldwide in temperate climates, thriving in places where few other plants can survive.

idTips.label: Growth Form
idTips.description: Forms distinctive rounded cushions or pillows on hard surfaces, with individual cushions ranging from coin-sized to palm-sized

idTips.label: Habitat
idTips.description: Almost exclusively grows on rocks, concrete walls, rooftops, and other hard, exposed surfaces rather than soil

idTips.label: Color
idTips.description: Grayish-green when dry, becoming brighter green when wet - the color change is quite dramatic after rain

idTips.label: Texture
idTips.description: Feels firm and slightly rough when dry, becoming soft and spongy when moistened

idTips.label: Leaves
idTips.description: Tiny, narrow leaves that curl inward when dry but spread out when wet, visible with a hand lens

idTips.label: Sporophytes
idTips.description: Small capsules on short stalks appear seasonally, often hidden within the cushion

habitat: Look for grey-cushioned grimmia on exposed rock faces, stone walls, concrete structures, and even rooftops throughout New England. It particularly favors limestone and concrete surfaces, thriving in sunny, dry locations where most other plants cannot survive. You'll often find it on cemetery headstones, bridge abutments, and the tops of stone walls.

seasonality.spring: Cushions begin to green up with spring rains, becoming more vibrant and noticeable. Sporophytes may begin developing during this wet season.
seasonality.summer: During dry periods, cushions appear grayish and contracted, but quickly green up after summer thunderstorms. This is when the dramatic color-change effect is most obvious.
seasonality.fall: Continues to show the wet-dry color changes with autumn rains. Sporophytes mature and release spores during this season.
seasonality.winter: Remains visible on rocks and walls even under snow, appearing gray-brown and dormant but ready to green up with the next thaw.

funFact: This tough little moss can survive being completely dried out for months, then spring back to life within minutes of getting wet - it's like nature's own resurrection plant, performing this amazing revival act right on your garden wall!
confusionNotes: Other rock mosses in the Grimmia genus can look similar, but grey-cushioned grimmia forms the most distinctive, well-rounded cushions. Remember: if it's growing in a perfect pillow shape on concrete or limestone, it's likely this species.
contextualKnowledge: Despite being called a 'rock moss,' this species particularly loves human-made surfaces like concrete and mortar, making it more common now than it was before widespread construction with lime-based materials.
compareHints: Unlike Grimmia Dry Rock Moss which tends to form flatter mats, grey-cushioned grimmia creates more pronounced, dome-shaped cushions. Donn's Grimmia is much rarer and typically found on acidic rocks rather than the limestone and concrete surfaces that grey-cushioned grimmia prefers. The cushion growth form is really the key distinguishing feature among the Grimmia species.

relatedSpecies.distinction: Grimmia Dry Rock Moss differs from Grey-cushioned Grimmia by having more pronounced white hair-tips and forming tighter, more dome-like cushions rather than looser mats.
Compared to Grey-cushioned Grimmia, Donn's Grimmia forms much smaller, more compact cushions and turns darker when dry.
